recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11162 unless Patient Care chooses to file a new editorial issue to restate the result-versus-reason distinction more explicitly after the CodeableReference refactor.
issue_request: FHIR-11162 was a Published Patient Care change request with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked how remedial treatments could be referenced when complications occurred, and the accepted disposition said remedial treatments can be represented as Procedures that are partOf another Procedure; Procedure.complication should support Condition references or a CodeableConcept; and the complication usage note should clarify that it documents a condition resulting from the procedure rather than the reason the procedure was performed.
initial_application: Git commit fd96fa1d81 applied the issue in the older split-element model by adding Procedure.complicationDetail as Reference(Condition) with the requested result-not-reason requirements text while retaining Procedure.complication as the coded concept location.
additional_context: Procedure is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issue FHIR-32511 merged Procedure.complication and Procedure.complicationDetail into Procedure.complication CodeableReference(Condition), and source/fhir.ini records that mapping. Current Procedure.reason separately captures why the procedure was performed, and current Procedure.complication is defined and bound as a resulting complication. Later FHIR-47824 only added isSummary=true for Procedure.complication.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scope source already provides Procedure.partOf for remedial procedures, Procedure.complication as CodeableReference(Condition) with coded text support, and separate Procedure.reason semantics; re-adding the old split-element usage sentence would be redundant.
